parts.text: A student prepares some crystals of pure potassium sulfate by reacting aqueous potassium carbonate with dilute sulfuric acid. The equation for the reaction is shown. K 2 CO 3 (aq) + H 2 SO 4 (aq) K 2 SO 4 (aq) + H 2 O(l) + CO 2 (g) The student: • places 25.0 cm 3 of aqueous potassium carbonate in a conical flask • adds a few drops of a suitable indicator to the conical flask • uses a burette to add dilute sulfuric acid to the conical flask until the end-point is reached and the indicator changes colour. Table 1.1 shows the burette readings the student obtains. Table 1.1 final burette reading / cm 3 18.8 initial burette reading / cm 3 4.2 volume of dilute sulfuric acid added / cm 3
